original_question: If a nontrivial classical knot is modified by virtualizing some crossings to produce a nontrivial virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial, can the resulting knot nevertheless be classical; can every virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial be related to a classical diagram by virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization; and if two classical knots differ by crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, must they already be classically equivalent?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 11, "Virtualization and Unit Jones Polynomial." ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact three-part scope of Problem 11: (1) start with a nontrivial classical knot, virtualize some crossings, and ask whether the resulting nontrivial unit-Jones virtual knot could still be classical; (2) ask whether any virtual knot with unit Jones polynomial is related to a classical diagram by virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization; and (3) ask whether crossing virtualization plus virtual Reidemeister moves can ever relate two genuinely different classical knot types. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's target is an open problem in Section 7, Problem 11, not a numbered conjecture or theorem from the introduction. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

In the first clause, the hypotheses are specifically: K is a classical knot, K is nontrivial, and \tilde K is obtained from K by virtualizing a subset of the crossings of K; \tilde K is itself assumed nontrivial. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The Jones-polynomial condition should be stated exactly as V(\tilde K)=1, or equivalently V_{\tilde K}(t)=1 in the notation introduced in Section 3. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

Crossing virtualization should be defined explicitly as replacing a classical crossing by a crossing flanked by two virtual crossings; the paper recalls this definition and notes that this operation does not affect the Jones polynomial. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

"Classical" in the first clause is clarified in the paper as being isotopic through virtual equivalence to a classical knot; Section 2 explains virtual equivalence via generalized Reidemeister moves together with the detour move. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The second clause is phrased in the paper for a virtual knot diagram K with unit Jones polynomial, asking whether K is equivalent to a classical diagram via virtual equivalence plus crossing virtualization. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The third clause is stated for classical knots K and K' and asks whether, if K is obtained from K' by a combination of crossing virtualization and virtual Reidemeister moves, then K and K' must already be classically equivalent. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper also records the intended consequence of these questions: affirmative answers would imply that the unknot is the only classical knot with unit Jones polynomial. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: Problem 11 (Virtualization and Unit Jones Polynomial): let crossing virtualization mean replacing a classical crossing by that crossing flanked by two virtual crossings. Determine whether the following assertions hold: (i) if K is a nontrivial classical knot and \tilde K is a nontrivial virtual knot obtained from K by virtualizing some subset of its crossings, with Jones polynomial V_{\tilde K}(t)=1, then \tilde K is not classical, i.e. it is not virtually equivalent to any classical knot; (ii) every virtual knot diagram K with unit Jones polynomial V_K(t)=1 is equivalent to a classical diagram by virtual equivalence together with crossing virtualization; and (iii) whenever classical knots K and K' are related by crossing virtualizations and virtual Reidemeister moves, they are already classically equivalent. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at Section 7, Problem 11 because it reproduces all three of that problem's questions in essentially the same order and with the same content. Section 3 supplies the motivation and hidden setup: the paper first explains that from any nontrivial classical knot diagram one can produce a nontrivial virtual knot diagram Virt(K) with unit Jones polynomial by virtualizing an unknotting subset of crossings, and Section 2 supplies the meaning of virtual equivalence. The refined version therefore keeps the problem narrow, uses the paper's own terminology, and makes explicit the definitions and hypotheses that are implicit in your draft. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

citations.label: Virtual Knot Theory (virtual equivalence via generalized Reidemeister moves and the detour move)
Theorem: to each non-trivial classical knot diagram of one component K there is a corresponding non-trivial virtual knot diagram Virt(K) with unit Jones polynomial
